scope: Same authorized mining project, payout address, 2 threads, CPU<=20%, process-group memory<=3072MB and cumulative single-run duration<=900s. Linux execution is isolated in an owned QEMU/WHPX VM, guest RAM2816MiB, with no host folder/clipboard sharing and restricted guest network. No new funds, signing, daily schedule or security-setting changes.
checks: Official pinned XMRig6.26 Linux release asset hash; extracted ELF independently hashed. Same scoped RandomX/CPU/pool/donation source review as the Windows route; this is not a full binary audit.

Copied and verified all364 hash-listed local vendor runtime files; did not modify another project or reuse its guest disk, seed, SSH key or wallet. This turn did not independently repeat each MSYS2 package signature verification.

Rehashed public Ubuntu24.04 minimal base image and matched publisher HTTPS SHA256SUMS for release20261105. Prior image-verification recorded a valid Ubuntu signature; this turn repeated the image hash and official checksum comparison.

Cloud-init seed contains only a newly generated public SSH key and OS settings. Private SSH key and authenticated miner-API configuration stay outside the save library. Guest never receives wallet credentials.

QEMU guest egress disabled. Host opens a fixed upstream rx.unmineable.com:443 gateway; SSH forwards only that pool and authenticated loopback miner status. No arbitrary caller-provided endpoints or commands.
Actual OS/SSH preflight returned prospect and x86_64 before any miner upload. All processes inherit the assigned Windows resource Job; stopping kills the VM and descendants.
limitations: Virtualization adds a boundary but does not guarantee absence of hypervisor, OS or miner vulnerabilities.
Pool SSL uses a first-use certificate pin, not independent CA authentication. User explicitly acknowledged this within the original mining authorization.
Tradability is verified; positive net profit is not promised. Accepted shares, custodial pool credit and actual chain receipt remain different outcomes.
